- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.5), model tends to overcorrect upward; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After sharp price spikes, model often overshoots downward; apply a 3–5 day lag correction to avoid premature drop.
- In mean-reverting regimes (sentiment neutral to slightly positive), model overestimates downward momentum; adjust downward bias by 2–5%.
- If sentiment is consistently positive (e.g., > 0.3), model tends to overestimate upward movement; cap forecast growth at 3–5% above recent high.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently underestimates downward trends in low-sentiment periods; add 1–3% buffer below true low.
- When sentiment swings sharply (e.g., +0.7 to -0.6), model misreads direction; align forecast with sentiment’s 2–3 day moving average instead of raw trend.
